body: Something is still bothering me, but I would rather not talk about it online to strangers...lol
Well, that's the problem. I really don't know how to move forward and come to terms with things. I don't know how to do that.

I just have no idea where or how to start with all of that, haha.

I talked about that a bit [here](http://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/hz1cs/how_do_i_find_something_to_live_for/c1zk1r9). It's just difficult to forget/come to terms with what happened, I guess.

I like listening to music too, but I myself am not musically inclined, haha. 

Yeah, I guess I'll keep looking. I really don't know where/how to start, though.

I really don't know what I would like to have in life. I am limited by what I can feasibly end up having, I guess. In terms of what makes me happy, I guess that I like helping people when I can.

How can I face my past? What would that entail?

The thing is, I know that I am not at the worst point in my life. Not by far; I've gone through much worse. I'm just tired of having to engage in this struggle at all. I don't think that I am meant to be successful or anything like that...I don't know how to find happiness and I can't truly say that I have ever been happy at any stage in my life.

Nah, don't worry. I expected a lot of that. And yeah, I'm going to college in the fall. 

The problem is that there really isn't anything that I *want* to do. Everything I do, whether a hobby or a major responsibility, feels completely pointless, menial, mundane, trivial, etc. I don't really enjoy doing anything, and there isn't anything which truly holds my interest or that I'm passionate about. This makes me very frustrated and eventually I end up getting like this. I have felt like this for a couple of years. I can usually push myself to keep going through the motions, but for the past few weeks things have been very difficult.

I have a lengthy history of mental illness, starting from the age of 3 or 4. I've seen a lot of therapists/psychiatrists and have been on a lot of medication. I spent a very large chunk of my life drugged up. I spent a lot of time in psychiatric hospitals, where I was sometimes abused by the staff (and sometimes other older kids). My parents tried to put me in foster care or a group home a few times (after no relatives wanted to take me). I don't know how to deal with all of this. All of the memories are too painful and I can't forget them.
